claim: Wake fitter than replaced tissue (paired-passage delta)
old: paired delta +0.95%, p < 1e-300 (n = 28,066 site-passages, treated iid)
corrected: delta = +0.951% (95% CI 0.91-0.99%); serial correlation (lag-1 rho = 0.59, corr. length ~33) -> n_eff ~ 3,300; block/run-clustered bootstrap SE 0.00020 vs naive 0.000069; worst case (150 run-scale blocks) t = 47.8, p ~ 3e-92
verdict: STILL SUPPORTED (decisively). The <1e-300 is unjustified pseudo-precision; report effect + corrected CI, drop the p-value.

claim: Excursion launches biased toward boundary-proximal beneficial events (launch-window bias)
old: 52.7% of 7,182 pre-launch events on launching side vs area-corrected null 50.4%; binomial p = 5e-5 (naive-null p = 2.5e-6)
corrected: events pooled across 2,010 excursions in 150 runs; events in one pre-launch window share that excursion's direction, so the excursion is the unit: 1,959 excursions carry >=1 event -> z = 2.04, one-sided p = 0.021; with run clustering (design effect 1.16, n_eff ~ 1,690) p = 0.029. Only ~half the excess survives if within-excursion correlation is partial (rho=0.5: p = 5e-3).
verdict: WEAKENED. Direction survives at p ~ 0.02-0.03 (not p ~ 1e-5). Restate as a modest, marginally significant bias; the 'not co-occurrence' framing still holds but the strength does not.

corrected: run-clustering weak (ICC = 0.04, design effect 1.5, n_eff ~ 1,318); run-clustered bootstrap 95% CI [30.4, 33.0] rows vs naive [30.4, 32.7]; median of per-run medians 33.6 (150 runs)
verdict: UNCHANGED. Descriptive median barely affected; quote 31.5 rows (95% CI 30-33, run-clustered).

claim: Arrest time not higher under load (9.5 +/- 0.8% vs 10.7 +/- 1.9%, n.s.)
corrected: already per-run: loaded 9.5 +/- 0.4% (SEM, n = 150 runs), neutral 10.7 +/- 1.0% (SEM, n = 20 runs); Welch t = -1.13, p = 0.27; Mann-Whitney p = 0.29. Manuscript SEs (0.8, 1.9) are ~2x the SEMs (likely SD-based), a conservative direction.
verdict: CORRECTLY REPLICATED, still n.s. Caveat to state: n = 20 neutral runs bounds the detectable difference (~3 percentage points).

run-level bootstrap on the persisted width-control trajectories (400 runs/condition): L_short=256, beta = 0.415 [0.406, 0.423]; L_short=128, beta = 0.387 [0.376, 0.398]. The fixation-ensemble CI [0.371,0.396] (width 0.025) is consistent with a run-level bootstrap, so it appears correctly computed.

verdict: STILL SUPPORTED. Attach the run-level CI to the control value: beta = 0.415 +/- 0.008 (well above KPZ 1/3 and EW 1/4).

claim: Gap variance growth Var[g] ~ t^alpha, alpha = 1.47-2.12 (six geometries)
old: alpha range quoted without CIs; sigma_dR per geometry with CIs (N = 1,536-24,576 gap samples)
corrected: Var[g](t) is an across-run variance at each t (run = unit) - the point estimates are properly replicated; a CI would require refitting under run bootstrap, which needs per-run g(t) (NOT persisted in the store). The independent A_load replicate ensemble (120 runs) gives alpha = 1.83, corroborating alpha ~ 2 (random slope) vs 1 (diffusion). The sigma_dR CIs and the 'N' labels count within-run frame increments, so those CIs are pseudo-replicated and TOO NARROW; run-level CIs cannot be recomputed from the store.
unit_new: run (150-200 per geometry) - NOT RECOMPUTABLE from persisted data
verdict: POINT ESTIMATES SUPPORTED; sigma_dR CIs SHOULD BE FLAGGED. The qualitative claim (alpha ~ 2, gap is a random slope) is robust; the anisotropic sigma_dR exponent fit (L^-0.74 L^-0.26) inherits over-narrow input CIs and its own CIs are optimistic.

claim: Freeze/flow ridge law s* ~ Lambda^0.48 and nested F-tests (p = 0.48, 1.4e-3, 1.8e-6)
old: OLS across 8-10 ridge points; F-tests on residual SS
corrected: each ridge point s* is itself a run-level bootstrap crossing (150 seeds/rung, 1,000 resamples) - the unit is the ridge point, which is a proper aggregate. The F-tests treat 8 points as independent; they are, because each ladder uses disjoint seeds. No pooling of within-run observations.
verdict: CORRECTLY REPLICATED. Not a pseudo-replication case.

claim: Intensivity of U_d/s_d: slope -0.02/decade [-0.22, +0.19], chi2 p = 0.60
corrected: each crossing mu_d* is a run-bootstrapped aggregate (150 runs/rung; largest cell 60 runs) - properly replicated. The defect is FRAMING (underpowered null), addressed in B3: detectable slope at 80% power is 0.28/decade; TOST excludes |slope| > 0.17/decade.
verdict: CORRECTLY REPLICATED but MISFRAMED: replace 'intensive' with the bounded statement (see B3).

claim: Excursion waiting times exponential with no aging
corrected: run-level within-run CV = 0.68 +/- 0.02 (mean over 136 runs; t vs exponential value 1: p < 1e-6) -> more regular than exponential (sub-Poissonian); per-run KS(expon) rejects in 9/101 runs; no aging confirmed: within-run Spearman rho(waiting, elapsed) = -0.01 +/- 0.03 (141 runs, p = 0.67)
verdict: SPLIT: 'no aging' SUPPORTED run-by-run; 'exponential' NOT supported at run level (CV 0.68 < 1) - rewrite as memoryless/no aging but more regular than Poisson.
